result: The old clock on the mantle ticks with a rhythm that feels like a heartbeat, though it has no blood to pump. Dust motes dance in the shaft of afternoon light, golden and weightless, suspended in a world that has forgotten to hurry. Here, in the quiet corner of the attic, time folds in on itself. A leather-bound journal lies open, its pages yellowed like autumn leaves. The ink is fading, but the words still hum with the emotion of the hand that wrote them a century ago. I trace the curve of a sentence, imagining the whisper that might have accompanied it. Was it a secret? A vow? A simple grocery list that became poetry through repetition? Outside, the wind rattles the windowpane, bringing the scent of pine and distant rain. It reminds me that the world is vast and wild, even when this room feels like a sealed capsule. There is a comfort in this stillness, a reminder that not everything needs to be solved or spoken. Sometimes, existence is just the sound of the clock, the dance of dust, and the quiet acceptance of the moment, fleeting. The leather creaks softly under my touch, a protest of age that sounds like a secret being whispered. Fingers of shadow lengthen across the floorboards, stretching toward the door as the sun begins its slow descent. The air grows cooler, carrying a sharper edge of pine needles and damp earth. I close my eyes and listen to the silence deepen.
